descriptions: St Helena is a remote territory, heavily reliant on the importation of goods, many of which contain plastic. Waste management facilities are very limited, meaning that waste can enter the marine environment whilst sitting in landfill.  The aim of this project was to improve waste management, monitor marine litter and social attitudes, and conduct public outreach. The project funded plastic recycling machines to support local businesses and artists to make and sell items from reused plastic. Additional disposal facilities were also installed. The monitoring section of the project allowed for the first surveys of beach litter and public perceptions of marine plastic on the island; building towards more sustainable resources management. The project also highlighted the unique challenges many Overseas Island Territories face, particularly their vulnerability to marine litter, which threatens key natural resources many island communities depend upon. St Helena and Defra hope that the project will deliver a legacy of sustainable behaviour and lead to further developments on island.

International Conference- NTFC: UNCTAD co-organized, together with the WCO, the International Trade Centre (ITC), the World Trade Organization (WTO) and the World Bank Group, the first ever International Forum for National Trade Facilitation Committees (NCTFs) at the United Nations headquarters in Geneva on the 23-27th of January 2017.  The objective of the Forum was to strengthen the capacities of NCTF representatives and to provide opportunities to access funding. The Forum covered various aspects related to the establishment and sustaining of NCTFs, including international best practices and coaching techniques. More than 300 delegates from 70 countries representing Ministries of Trade, Customs Administrations, the Private Sector, Customs Administrations, Regional Organizations and International Organizations participated in the Forum of which 13 national delegations were sponsored by the HMRC-Programme (Democratic Republic of Congo, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Jordan, Liberia, Malawi, Mozambique, Pakistan, Palestine, Sierra Leone, Sudan and Zimbabwe.)

titles: Trade Facilitation - HR development and TFA competencies
descriptions: HR development and TFA competencies: In response to a specific request from Palestine Customs, the WCO organized a workshop to support Palestinian Customs in modernizing and reforming their Human Resource Management (HRM) to adopt a competency based approach and better aligns the administrations procedures with international standards including the TFA. The workshop provided an opportunity for participants to discuss the strategic role of HRM in a broader development perspective. Participants also gained an increased understanding of specific HRM measures including the development of a job catalog, a competency based framework, a competency dictionary and certain job descriptions. As a result of the workshop, recommendations were developed on how to move the HRM modernization process forward.  Further support on how to finalize the design of competency based approach tools will be provided remotely by the WCO.

Risk Management: In response to a specific request from Palestine Customs, the WCO delivered a Risk Management assessment workshop to strengthen the capacities and increase efficiency of the administrations Risk Management Unit to better comply with the requirements of the TFA.
The workshop provided a general introduction to basic concepts of Customs Risk Management including Risk assessment profiling, targeting concept and benefits, basic elements of compliance management as well as an introduction in use of intelligence sources.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Single Window Compendium- Updated
descriptions: Single Window Compendium- Updated: Development work for the new Single Window e-learning module continues on schedule, with an expected launch of the pilot version of the product in mid-2017.  Plans for the piloting of the new product in Bangladesh and Malawi, where critical decisions related to National Single Window projects are being deliberated.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Monitoring and update of Mercator plan
descriptions: Monitoring and update of Mercator plan: To assess the outcomes and impact of HMRC-supported investments in Palestine since April 2016, and to identify a forward plan under the tailor-made track of the Mercator Programme, the WCO completed a Monitoring and Evaluation mission in Ramallah. The WCO mission team made a positive assessment of previous WCO interventions, including support on Strategic planning, Risk Management, Human Resource development support and improved participation and engagement with the private sector. The mission allowed the WCO to get an improved understanding of the work of other development partners in Palestine and a clear understanding of Palestine’s forward priorities for technical assistance, largely focused on gaining exposure to “live” Customs clearance facilities that they lack in the current political context and also refined objectives for continued Mercator engagement in Palestine, focusing on apolitical, technical exposure and further exposure / possible accession to the RKC, and close collaboration with other development partners.

LMD: Based on the draft 2017 Mercator Implementation Plan for Palestine, the WCO facilitated a Leadership Management and Development (LMD) workshop for 16 senior and middle managers to enhance their skills on how to effectively implement Customs reforms through effective change management in practice in order to comply with international standards such as the TFA and impending changes to the Palestinian reality, given emerging agreements with Israel. During the workshop, participants were exposed to relevant aspects of leadership such as visioning, people management, delegation, motivation, negotiations, communications, integrity, diversity - and change management, all of which will be essential in helping Palestine to face significant changes to its policy and procedural realities.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Customs Control and Bonded Warehouse
descriptions: Customs Control and Bonded Warehouse: Based on the approved 2017 Mercator Implementation Plan for Palestine the WCO organized a working visit to Morocco to help Palestine to better understand the bonded warehouse concept.  The Palestinian Customs administration is working with their Israeli counterparts to establish a bonded warehouse concept in Palestine, which will shift much of the responsibility for clearing goods from Israeli to Palestinian authorities.  The establishment of a bonded warehouse as a form of “border” where all relevant Palestinian border agencies would be represented alongside the private sector is an entirely new concept for Palestine.  Morocco’s bonded warehouse system is considered to be a regional best practice, and Palestine’s increased understanding of the procedures for establishing such a facility, including benefits, processes and Customs’ role in supervision and regulation will better prepare for the rapid pace of change that will be taking place in their own Customs territory.  Advice from Morocco will encourage Palestine to uphold TFA standards on coordinated border management, risk management and post-clearance audit in the new concept.  The WCO continues to engage with Palestine and key donor organizations therein to ensure to most effective and consistent advice is provided to Palestine

PCA: Also based on the approved 2017 Mercator Implementation Plan for Palestine, the WCO completed a post-clearance audit (PCA) diagnostic aiming at identifying specific capacity building needs allowing the establishment of an effective PCA function for Palestinian Customs, in line with the requirements of Article 7.5 of the TFA. The diagnostic allowed Customs officers from different departments to gain an increased understanding of the basic concepts of PCA, relevant policy development and its relation to other Customs areas including risk management, audit phases and human resource requirements. The diagnostic also included discussions with Directors from different divisions, expected to be involved in the PCA implementation. To better understand the situation of private stakeholders a meeting was organized at the headquarters of the Palestinian Customs gathering five of the most important importers in Palestine, the Chamber of Commerce and key Customs brokers. The mission was considered as a milestone in building and developing results oriented support for effective PCA implementation in Palestine. It resulted in a clear understanding of the importance of PCA as well as the benefits of establishing an independent PCA function.

titles: Trade Facilitation - National Trade Facilitation Committees(NTFC) Regional Workshop
descriptions: National Trade Facilitation Committees(NTFC) Regional Workshop: The third module of the NTFC Empowerment Programme, focusing on the establishment of a trade facilitation roadmap, was delivered by UNCTAD and gathered 34 participants. The workshop, which was opened by Mr Stephen Marvie, Assistant Minister for Commerce and Trade Services provided an opportunity for participants to gain a better understanding of the TFA and the next steps required for the ratification, categorization, notification and implementation of the agreement in Liberia. Through a practical exercise, participants were also allowed to draft a roadmap under the guidance of UNCTAD.  Finally, the workshop included a preparatory session for Module 4 of the NTFC Empowerment Programme, planned to be delivered in January 2018. The draft Roadmap was completed by the UNCTAD team while back in Headquarters.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Leadership Management Development workshop
descriptions: Leadership Management Development workshop :In support of the Mercator Implementation Plan for Bangladesh, and an identified need to strengthen the skills of the management of the National Board of Revenue (NBR), the WCO delivered a workshop on Leadership and Management development benefiting a group of 20 senior managers of the NBR. The workshop provided an opportunity for the management officials to reflect on their own leadership and management perspectives. It also allowed the management to strengthen the team spirit to enable them to drive the modernization and reform agenda to support trade facilitation. Participants also gained an increased understanding of modern practices in Customs management and leadership, as outlined in the WCO PICARD professional standards.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Capacity Building Knowledge event
descriptions:
Capacity Building Knowledge event: To consolidate the efforts under the tailor-made track of the Mercator Programme and increase understanding among Priority countries for the WCO work on trade facilitation and capacity building, 14 Customs officials from Ethiopia, Jordan, Palestine, Sierra Leone, Sudan and Zimbabwe (all priority countries of the HMRC-Programme) and 1 MPA from Uganda engaged in the Mercator implementation for Afghanistan, participated in the TFA Working group, the CBC and the Integrity Sub Committee organized in Brussels on the week of 6th of March.

They also benefitted from joint sessions with the TFA Working group and the Integrity Sub-Committee to ensure alignment with trade facilitation and integrity perspectives. Moreover, delegations got the opportunity to share their views with Secretariat officials and other stakeholders in informal settings.

Project Management Training: Following the recommendations established for several core priority countries including Zimbabwe and Sierra Leone the WCO facilitated training on Project Management and Performance Measurement. The overall aim of this workshop was to enhance the capacities of Customs Administrations to effectively design and manage Reform and Modernization initiatives in order to become self-sustainable in the implementation of international standards while ensuring sustainability. The training was the first pilot workshop based on material developed by the WCO covering basic concepts of Project Management, an introduction to Organizational Project Management Framework (OPM) and Results Based Management including development of indicators and monitoring frameworks.

Time Release Study(TRS): In line with the Mercator Implementation Plan established for Ethiopia, the WCO completed a mission to reconfirm the commitment and update the planning framework for continued implementation of Mercator support. 
The core mandate of this mission, a transit diagnostic, did not take place since the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) confirmed at a late stage that they would support parallel work in the undertaking a Time Release Study (TRS) at these border stations.  ERCA therefore considered the mission to be redundant and requested it to be cancelled. Nevertheless, ERCA’s commitment to the Mercator implementation plan was reconfirmed and improved operating modalities in terms of mission planning, communication and priority setting were established.  The assigned Mercator Programme Advisor (MPA) will continue to work with ERCA to support the continued delivery of the Mercator Implementation Plan.  Clarity was also received on ERCA’s January 2017 request to the Finland ESA programme, allowing for the incorporation of key elements of this proposal into the main Mercator plan.

PCA for Trainers (Vol2): Following the Mercator Implementation Plan established for Ethiopia, and as part of its seven main priorities, the WCO completed a PCA diagnostic mission to identify specific capacity support needs in the area of PCA. The diagnostics included discussions with directors from different divisions within ERCA, including IT, legal, Risk Management, Customs Processing, Border Management, Valuations and local PCA teams. Moreover, visits were conducted to the Bole Airport and Kaliti Inland Port to understand the clearance processes and the links to PCA activities. The mission also included discussions with private stakeholders, on the role of the PCA function and their expectations. The mission resulted in a proposed action plan presenting recommendations on forward PCA support to be delivered under Ethiopia’s Mercator Implementation Plan.

titles: Trade Facilitation - TFA related competencies and Rules of Origin Diagnostic
descriptions:
TFA related competencies and Rules of Origin Diagnostic: In line with the Mercator Implementation Plan for Ethiopia, WCO delivered a 
Revenue Package workshop on the Advanced Ruling System for 
Classification and Origin which plays a vital role in promoting trade facilitation 
(Article 3.1). The aim of the workshop was to identify specific needs for Ethiopia in the development of an Advance Ruling system for classification and origin, to assess their current national tariff classification and origin work model and to provide information on the Advanced Ruling programme. The workshop allowed participants to strengthen their knowledge in Advance Rulings, including tools and instruments under the Revenue Package and the practical application of the Diagnostic Tool on Tariff Classification, Valuation, Origin Work and Related Infrastructure. As a result of the workshop proposals and solutions related to modernization of classification and origin work and to the implementation of an Advance Ruling system were developed.

TRS Methodology: In line with the National Mercator Plan for Ethiopia to support the Article 7.6 of the TFA, the WCO supported the finalization of a Time-Release Study (TRS) which is currently done under the framework of a regional programme under COMESA guidance. The objectives of this mission were twofold, both to provide technical assistance enabling Ethiopia to effectively critique and COMESA-led TRS, to successfully conclude the TRS process, and to strengthen the knowledge of local Customs officers allowing them to conduct future TRS for ERCA without external support. The support from the WCO focused on elements that were not properly considered in the preparations of the TRS but vital in order to comply with the expectations of COMESA and the latest WCO TRS guidance.

titles: Trade Facilitation - update of competency in intelligence-driven risk management and organisational RM
descriptions: update of competency in intelligence-driven risk management and organisational RM: Following the Mercator Implementation Plan for Ethiopia, WCO delivered a workshop to undertake a full diagnostic review of ERCA’s work on Risk management (RM) to identify current needs and develop recommendations for forward reform and modernization activities to support the implementation of Article 7.4 of the TFA.  This mission took into account the lackluster results of a generic World Bank-led risk management workshop in March 2017, and focused on Ethiopia’s particular needs and circumstances.  The mission included meetings with a number of concerned departments (Risk Management unit, IT, Intelligence, Legal, Procedures and Human Resources among others). Moreover, visits were made to the Bole Main Airport and to the Modjo Inland Port to study how intelligence based risk management supports trade facilitation and security. The WCO team of experts also analyzed the supply chain movement of goods from Djibouti Port transiting through the Galafi Border to the Inland Container Ports.  As a result of the mission, a detailed diagnostic and draft action plan for forward capacity building support related to Risk Management was developed. The outcomes of the mission were also presented to the Management of ERCA.

PCA operational guidance: Following the results of the previous PCA Diagnostic completed in February 2017 and in line with the National Mercator Implementation Plan for Ethiopia, the WCO delivered a PCA-training supporting ERCA to gain knowledge and skills in how to implement PCA in accordance to the WCO PCA Guidelines. The training provided participants, including PCA Managers and Operational Auditors, with Customs Audit technical skills which will enable them to execute PCA audits using a system based audit approach, which is core to the facilitative Customs-to-business partnership principles of PCA. It also included practical case studies related to valuation. The experience from this training is planned to serve as a basis to update ERCA’s current PCA manual.  
In addition, on occasion of the ICAO meeting on Air Cargo Development organized in Addis on the 27-29 of June, a WCO Valuation expert took the opportunity to engage with the ERCA Valuation Directorate to prepare a Valuation Infrastructure Diagnostic proposed in the framework of the Mercator Plan

titles: Trade Facilitation - TRS review and Business procedures from Djbouti
descriptions: TRS review and Business procedures from Djbouti: Based on the Mercator Implementation Plan for Ethiopia and following a specific request from Ethiopian Revenue and Customs Authority (ERCA), the WCO and UNCTAD jointly carried out a combined time release study and coordinated border management mission to increase ERCA’s internal capacities in these two areas. The aim of the mission was to complete a TRS along Ethiopia’s major goods movement corridor (from Djibouti Port through Galafi Border post up to Addis Ababa container deport) to analyze the regulatory clearance and release process involving all government agencies and logistic providers, in keeping with the requirements of the WTO TFA. By applying a structured methodology, the mission resulted in a comprehensive analysis and documentation of the clearance process at three Ethiopian Customs stations which will help designing the Business Process Map needed to carry out future TRSs along Ethiopia’s major ports. Moreover, ERCA officials gained an increased understanding of the TRS methodology and its associated activities including process mapping, as well as the importance of close collaboration with other government agencies to succeed with Coordinated Border Management reforms and Single Window implementation. Linkages between other WCO-led Mercator programme activities including Risk Management, AEO and PCA were highlighted throughout the mission as well as the strategic alignment with the overall Mercator Implementation Plan.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Advance Ruling potential mandate
descriptions: Advance Ruling potential mandate: Based on the Mercator Implementation Plan for Ethiopia, and following a first Valuation diagnostic completed in May 2017, the WCO delivered a second workshop to strengthen ERCAs knowledge and capacities in the area of classification and origin. The workshop aimed at assisting ERCA in developing a mandate for establishing an Advance Rulings unit, including defining roles and responsibilities. This unit is meant to act as a center of knowledge on classification and rules of origin in keeping with Article 3.1 of the WTO TFA. The workshop also provided guidance related to the legislation for the Advance Rulings Unit and provided an introduction to the theoretical and practical aspects of implementing an advance ruling programme. Participants also had an opportunity to discuss best practices around organising tariff classification, origin work and related infrastructure.  ERCA is now positioned to action some of the first advance rulings requests from the private sector.

Advanced Rulings: To better comply with the requirements of international standards, including the TFA, the WCO delivered a national workshop to support Jordan’s Customs Administration in implementing an Advance Ruling System, particularly in the area of tariff classification of goods. The workshop included an assessment of the specific needs and problems of Jordan Customs related to implementation of Advance Rulings systems and an assessment of the national model of tariff classification. Participants gained an increased understanding of both the theoretical and practical aspects of the implementation of Advance Ruling systems. They also discussed best practices on classification work, origin and related infrastructure to determine forward procedures and establish an action plan. This workshop was partly funded by the HMRC programme in line with the Programme objectives to support Jordan Customs.

Performance Management- HR: In response of a specific request from Jordan Customs, the WCO supported Jordan Customs to review its organizational performance indicators. The workshop included guidance on how to implement a Balanced Scorecard (BSC), methodology for monitoring and reporting on performance, as well as an introduction of key Customs performance indicators. The workshop also provided examples of good international experiences in designing, collecting, analysing, using and publishing performance information to support Jordan Custom’s strategic direction, reform and modernization actions to better comply with the requirements of international standards such as the TFA. Moreover, the workshop helped Jordan Customs in the development of new indicators in line with the updated Strategic Plan for their Administration which includes several key WTO TFA priorities. This workshop was partly funded by the HMRC programme in line with the Programme objectives to support Jordan Customs.

Participants were also provided with some best practices in terms of establishing, managing an NTFC and introduction to steps that countries are expected to take prior and after WTO TFA entry into force. Risk Management: Also based on the 2017 Mercator Implementation Plan for Malawi, the WCO completed a Risk Management diagnostic to review the MRA’s current procedures, identify gaps and develop recommendations for forward reform and modernization activities to support the implementation of Article 7.4 of the WTO TFA, and further risk management activities under the Mercator Plan. 
Through informed and collaborative discussions with Senior officials from different departments (Risk Management, IT, Intelligence, Legal, Procedures, HR among others) the WCO team completed a comprehensive review of the MRA’s Risk Management policy, strategy and infrastructure. The mission team also shared regional best practices on risk-based analytics for the different units. As a result of the mission, the different units of the MRA increased their knowledge on how to develop risk profiles using archived data, in establishing intelligence units and in strengthening Risk Management processes and capabilities in line with international standards and best practices, in particular the TFA.  A detailed diagnostic report further detailing the proposals from the 2017 Mercator Plan were presented to the MRA senior team.  This mission was also co-financed by the Finland ESA programme.

NTFC Module 2: Module 2 of the NTFC Empowerment Programme focusing on “Measuring and Implementing Trade Facilitation” was organized in Nigeria in collaboration with a GIZ-UNCTAD project in the region. The workshop gathered more than 40 Nigerian stakeholders, both from the public and private sectors.  The workshop covered an introduction to approaches for monitoring and evaluating the progress of national trade facilitation reforms, including the Result Based Management approach. Participants were also provided an introduction to the role of Single Window (SW) as a catalyzer in facilitating trade facilitation reforms, including methods to analyze, monitor and evaluate the impacts of SW. 
The workshop also focused on the Nigerian Trade Information Portal, particularly its role in leveraging national trade facilitation reforms. Participants also gained an increased understanding of the Supply Chain perspective in assessing country needs for trade facilitation reforms and the Business Process Analysis (BPA) approach to measure and benchmark the problem. 
Participants were also introduced in some trade facilitation measured including Authorized Economic Operators (AEO) and Advance Ruling, as examples of relatively less complicated measures to implement in order to mitigate border delays. The workshop also included group exercises to adapt the contents of the workshop to the specific case of Nigeria.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Data model alignment with Wboc
descriptions: Data model alignment with Wboc: Following a specific request from Pakistan, to support their newly initiated Single Window Project (in line with Article 10.4 TFA), the WCO delivered a workshop on Data Model for the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR). Unlike other priority countries, Pakistan has developed its own “home-grown” Customs management system, and has considerable IT capacity to manage its continued growth and connection to other government agencies. The workshop aimed at strengthening FBR’s skills to map national data requirements to international standards and develop capacities to undertake data harmonization to support Single Window. The workshop provided participants with an increased understanding of WCO Data Model concepts and improved skills on how to establish a reliable, harmonized and standardized platform for electronic exchange with all value chain stakeholders both nationally and internationally.

PCA Diagnostic: Building on the outcomes of the Programme’s January 2017 engagement at a joint TFA assessment workshop, the WCO organized a PCA diagnostic in Pakistan with the objective to complete a comprehensive review of the current PCA policies, strategy, infrastructure and implementation processes to ensure alignment with international standards, in particular Article 7.5 of the TFA. The workshop also aimed at identifying the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) needs and forward recommendations for PCA reforms in order to develop a Pakistani-led action plan to establish an efficient PCA function, which could be passed to other development partners for long-term support. Through plenary sessions, a study visit to the Islamabad Dry Port and meetings with six of the largest importers and exporters in Pakistan, the mission team completed a comprehensive assessment of the current situation. During the mission, the FBR recognized the critical importance of maintaining an effective PCA function in order to enhance trade facilitation whilst ensuring effective Customs control and increased compliance.  As a result of the diagnostic, several recommendations on how to assist the FBR in enhancing its PCA function were identified. Moreover, the FBR gained an increased understanding of how to seek further support from domestic and international stakeholders in order to implement effective PCA.

Scoping/Needs Assessment: In coordination with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), UNCTAD and the International Trade Centre (ITC), WCO co-sponsored a National Workshop to support Pakistan in implementing the TFA. The workshop was opened by the Minister of Commerce in Pakistan, H. E. Engr. Khurram Dastgir Khan and gathered around 50 participants from different government agencies and private sector associations. This multi-stakeholder workshop was designed to support Pakistan in the development of implementation plans for selected TFA measures, while also supporting general awareness of the TFA and its benefits. The WCO used the opportunity to engage directly with the Federal Board of Revenue to discuss opportunities to provide forward Customs-to-Customs collaboration under the auspices of the tailor-made track of the Mercator Programme.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Ncen installation/Risk Management Coordination
descriptions: Ncen installation/Risk Management Coordination: Following the deployment of the nCEN (national Customs Enforcement Network) tool in Sierra Leone, the WCO delivered training for Customs officers on the functionality of this system. The nCEN is an intelligence gathering and analysis system allowing Customs Administrations to enhance their targeting and enforcement capacities by gathering information that can be transformed into risk indicators, thereby supporting the implementation of Article 7.4 (Risk Management) of the TFA.  The training allowed participants to gain knowledge on how to effectively use the nCEN tool and provided them with skills to start using the tool to target high-risk consignments with immediate effect, ultimately allowing for the facilitated movement of low-risk cargo. Moreover, the training prepared participants to assume responsibility for future management of the application at national level and with skills to transfer the knowledge to other national users. In the medium term perspective the use of nCEN system as a centralized database is expected to improve operational efficiency, analytical possibilities and to exchange information with other countries in keeping with the coordinated border management provisions of the TFA.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Introduction to Post Audit Clearance (PCA) and Operational Guidance
descriptions: Introduction to Post Audit Clearance (PCA) and Operational Guidance: Following the Mercator Implementation Plan established for Sierra Leone, the WCO delivered a mission to assess the status of the PCA functions of Sierra Leone and provide an introduction to WCO PCA Operational guidelines. A diagnostic of the National Revenue Authority’s current Post Clearance Audit (PCA) function was completed to identify gaps with the aim to support the administration to better understand and implement the PCA in line with the WCO PCA Guidelines. The mission also allowed identifying training needs related to PCA which will help the Programme to better adapt forward interventions to the needs of the Administration. The mission resulted in the development of a roadmap on how to coordinate the collaboration between staff from the risk management unit and the PCA unit.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Identification of practical solutions to automate existing risk profling / nCEN installation
descriptions: Identification of practical solutions to automate existing risk profling / nCEN installation: Also based on the 2016 Mercator Implementation Plan for Sierra Leone, and following recommendations from a WCO-led valuation diagnostic mission completed in September 2016, the WCO conducted a second workshop for the NRA to strengthen its Customs valuation training capacity in preparation for the planned termination of destination inspection contracts in 2019. The workshop included both theoretical sessions on valuation issues and practical exercises to improve participants’ training delivery skills. Moreover, each participant was given the opportunity to make a presentation on a Customs valuation topic.  The long-term objective of this assistance is to increase the NRA’s internal valuation capacities to enable them to assume the functions of the existing destination inspection company.  The elimination of destination inspection is a priority for the WCO, meets the requirements of the TFA’s article 10.6 and reduces costs and delays associated with international trade.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Support in Analysis/Publication of TRS
descriptions:
Support in Analysis/Publication of TRS: Two time-release study missions were delivered in this quarter, one in Ethiopia (to support the finalization of a TRS) and one in Bangladesh (to support the preparations of conducting a TRS).  
Similar engagements are currently being prepared for in core priority countries Zimbabwe, Sierra Leone and Sudan as well as Malawi.  
Completed studies in Sudan and Bangladesh have been analyzed for potential follow-up, review and actions, particularly as they relate to building local analytical capacity and the transparent publication of results.

PCA introduction: Also, based on the 2016 Mercator Implementation Plan for Sudan, the WCO completed a Post Clearance Audit (PCA) diagnostic in Sudan aiming at identifying specific capacity building needs allowing the establishment of an effective PCA function in line with the requirements of Article 7.5 of the TFA. The around 100 Customs officials from different departments who participated in the workshop, gained an increased understanding of basic concepts of PCA, relevant policy development, risk management, audit phases and human resource requirements for PCA. In order to understand the situation of private stakeholders, the mission team also met with five of the most important importers in Sudan and key Customs brokers. The mission resulted in a clear understanding of the importance of PCA as well as benefits of establishing an independent PCA function.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Support 2nd Risk Management piloting/diagnostic
descriptions: Support 2nd Risk Management piloting/diagnostic: Also, based on the 2016 Mercator Implementation Plan for Sudan, the WCO carried out a diagnostic to assess the capacities of Sudan Customs’ Risk management function as it moves to further roll-out risk management to other ports-of-entry.  The mission resulted in a clear understanding of the challenges, successes and constraints the Administration is currently facing in their efforts to implement a modern, intelligence-based Risk Management function in line with Article 7.5 of the TFA. The mission included visits to Khartoum International Airport (the pilot site for risk management for Sudan Customs), Soba Dry Port (the largest Customs clearance office in Sudan), the Legal administration, the IT department and other Customs administration offices. The diagnostic concluded in a number of forward recommendations based on five areas; risk management policy, strategic planning, intelligence, compliance, clearance and human resources which will form the basis for continued reforms in the area of Risk management.

HR Follow up: Building on the December 2016 human resources management work, a follow-up was facilitated upon request of Sudan Customs, and as a follow-up to the national workshop that took place in December 2016, the WCO facilitated a Human Resources Management (HRM) workshop aiming at evaluating the work initiated early 2017 and to come up with proposals on how to improve HRM tools. Improving Human Recourse capacities facilitates Administrations abilities to implement reforms and change management which in turn enables overall compliance with the TFA. The workshop resulted in the establishment of a HRM working group and the development of a forward-looking road map including a set of expected outcomes to fulfill HRM reform and modernization objectives. Moreover, the process of developing a HRM strategy, policy as well as competency based tools was also initiated. Finally, the workshop provided an opportunity for the participants to refresh and strengthen their skills and knowledge in the fields of staff planning, job descriptions, competency framework, performance assessment, staff motivation and development.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Monitoring and update of Mercator plan
descriptions: Monitoring and update of Mercator plan: To assess the outcomes and impact of HMRC-supported investments made in Zimbabwe since March 2016, the WCO completed a one week monitoring and formative evaluation mission. In addition, this mission also aimed at reviewing Zimbabwe’s global needs assessment for 2017, to identify next steps and to engage Zimbabwe in the development of a new Mercator implementation plan to facilitate TFA Implementation. The main focus was to leverage on previous investments in order to minimize any future duplications and ensure sustainability of WCO and HMRC investments in Zimbabwe. The new Mercator Implementation plan will be designed to be supported both by the HMRC-Programme and other WCO Capacity Building Programmes

titles: Trade Facilitation - In-country research to confirm to categorisation
descriptions: In-country research to confirm to categorisation: Based on the 2017 Mercator Implementation Plan for Zimbabwe, the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority’s (ZIMRA) training center saw the renewed integration of WCO e-learning modules as part of a blended learning approach in ZIMRA’s training programmes. The training workshop included a train-the-trainers session to introduce the blended learning approach, which combines e-learning material and face to face training. ZIMRA’s existing Training Strategy, Policy and Competency framework were also reviewed to ensure alignment with the WCO Customs Competency-Based Training Guidelines. ZIMRA expects to re-launch the new blended learning programme, incorporating TFA-related e-learning modules by the end of 2017.

NTFC Module 2: Module 2 of the NTFC Empowerment Programme focusing on “Measuring and Implementing Trade Facilitation” was organized in Nigeria in collaboration with a GIZ-UNCTAD project in the region. The workshop gathered more than 40 Nigerian stakeholders

titles: Trade Facilitation - Introduction to PCA and operational Guidance
descriptions: Introduction to PCA and operational Guidance: Based on the 2016 Mercator Implementation Plan for Zimbabwe, the WCO facilitated a workshop to strengthen the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA)’s knowledge and capacities on Post Clearance Audit (PCA) to enable better compliance with Article 7.5 of the TFA.  In total 15 representatives from various Customs units including PCA, Risk Management and Enforcement, gained an increased understanding of the importance of PCA as an integrated part of customs Risk Management strategy and processes in order to increase efficiency of controls and promote trade facilitation. The workshop also provided an opportunity for participants to practically implement PCA using a system based audit approach. Participants also practiced interview techniques to better understand auditable business processes and systems used by large multinationals. Finally, the workshop included a fruitful discussion with ZIMRA’s PCA management around developing an action plan to assist the Administration in enhancing their PCA function.

TRS Introduction :Also, based on the 2016 Mercator Implementation Plan for Zimbabwe, the WCO delivered a workshop to increase the country’s capacity to effectively and independently complete WCO Time Release Studies in support of the provisions of Article 7.6 of the TFA. The workshop allowed participants, including Customs officials, other Government Agencies - and private sector representatives, to gain an increased understanding of the WCO TRS methodology and provided an opportunity for ZIMRA to present some of their previous work to measure bottlenecks. The workshop also included a visit to the international Cargo Terminal, to study the Terminal importation process, as well as the management of the cargo process. As a result of the workshop, a roadmap on how to conduct a TRS was drafted by the participants. This roadmap will be used to guide Customs and other stakeholders to successfully and independently complete a TRS, as well as publishing the results, in 2018.

titles: Trade Facilitation - E-learning and Training strategy workshop
descriptions: E-learning and Training strategy workshop: Based on the updated 2017 Mercator Implementation Plan for Zimbabwe, the WCO organized a technical workshop at the Customs Training Academy to re-integrate WCO e-Learning modules as a blended approach in ZIMRA’s training programmes. The workshop focused on the installation and setup of an e-Learning platform including new TFA related modules, addressing risk management, coordinated border management and PCA. It also covered a train-the trainers’ session targeted for local Customs experts and facilitators to introduce the new tool and explain how it can be used as part of blended training programmes. Moreover, the Administration’s existing training strategy, - policy and competency framework were reviewed in line with the WCO Customs Competency-Based Training Guidelines.

NTFC module 0: Module 1 of the NTFC Empowerment Programme focusing on key trade facilitation concepts (i.e. simplification, harmonization, standardization, transparency) was delivered in Zimbabwe in January 2017 gathering around 50 participants from the Ministry of Trade, Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA) and private stakeholders. The workshop covered key international standards and instruments of both the WCO (SAFE Framework of Standards, WCO Data Model, Revised Kyoto Convention (RKC) ) and the TFA.  NTFC members and potential members acquired in-depth knowledge of the TFA and related international standards and instruments. In particular, participants gained an increased understanding of the links between the TFA and the RKC, SAFE standards as well as Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) and Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures (SPS) standards managed by WTO. 
The workshop also provided an opportunity to initiate the process to further institutionalize the NTFC, and guide the NTFC in taking the lead in preparing for Category C project proposals. In this context, a review of Zimbabwe’s forward need towards TFA implementation was completed and UNCTAD identified the following opportunities for forward support including the following: 
(1) support on the institutionalization process of Zimbabwe’s NTFC (establishment of its ToR and decree), 
(2) Organizing an executive awareness session senior management officials, planned to be completed in connection with the delivery of the next module.  
(3) National Border Agency coordination support and review of Category A measures to verify its implementation.

titles: Trade Facilitation - Introduction to Post Audit Clearance (PCA)
descriptions: Introduction to Post Audit Clearance (PCA): In support of the Mercator Implementation Plan for Zimbabwe, the WCO delivered a workshop to assess Zimbabwe’s existing PCA system and develop recommendations to strengthen ZIMRA’s role as part of a broader reform and modernization package to comply with the provisions of the TFA. The objectives of this mission were to increase the understanding among ZIMRA’s PCA staff on the WCO instruments and tools related to PCA and to raise understanding for PCA as a facilitative measure. The recommendations developed following the mission also covered parallel efforts in risk management and Authorized Economic Operators (AEO). The mission resulted in the development of a forward plan for further PCA engagement under the tailor-made track of the Mercator Programme

agency: Department for Environment Food and Rural Affairs
descriptions: During her visit to Kenya in August 2018, Theresa May launched a UK partnership with UN Environment to develop a Young Leaders Plastic Challenge Badge. In Phase 1 the programme developed the training material for a plastic challenge badge, this was then undertaken in four African countries (Ghana, Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania). Over 30,000 young leaders engaged in the programme which saw a real impact in countries like Kenya, Tanzania and Ghana where Scouts were actively involved in influencing national policy change about legislation around single-use plastic bags. Phase 2 aims to build upon the work successfully completed in phase 1, by reaching communities in many of the countries with the greatest issues with plastic pollution. The programme will expand the badge into a further 15 countries engaging up to an additional 300,000 young people and leave a legacy for the future years. Empowering young people remains a priority for the UK Government, and through HMG’s international work on marine litter, we have an opportunity to inspire young leaders in tackling marine plastic pollution. Now that the success of badge has been demonstrated through the pilot phase, there is a platform to secure deeper participation in other key countries in Africa and Asia Pacific. This work supports the UK’s domestic and global leadership to eliminate all avoidable single use plastics as set out in the HMG’s 25 Year Environment Plan and work with other countries to drive global ambition to protect and enhance the world’s oceans in support of UN SDG 14. Raising public awareness and effecting behaviour change is a key component of the global effort to reduce plastic pollution. Young people are a key demographic to engage, and one that we currently struggle to reach. The Scouts and Girl guiding Associations are uniquely placed to do this outreach, with combined total global membership of 65 million young people.
